actions.label: What does the order say?
actions.text:
Hollis: Grain for the far-bank households, sent under emergency provision. They were promised it three days ago.
Under the provision, the crossing counts as open when the marker reads open. The marker reads open.
Maelin: Marker's wrong.

actions.label: Why won't you cross?
actions.text:
Maelin: See the posts down the bank? Grey ones. Same notch, same height on every one.
Water over the notch, boots on the bank. That's the rule. Has been since before him.
Now look at the yellow one. That post wasn't there yesterday.

actions.label: So how do we settle this?
actions.text:
Hollis: If the marker's false, prove it. Show me, and I'll write it down and shut the crossing myself.
Maelin: Go and look at that post. Properly. Then talk to whoever's been on this bank longest.

actions.label: Did you see anything last night?
actions.text:
Nan: At dusk the posts were all grey, all the same. Water over every notch, so I sat down.
At first light there's a yellow one. Like a new tooth.
My mam had a rhyme for crossings. 'Mind the stone and not the stake; the stake is only what men make.'

actions.label: Could the carter have moved the post?
actions.text: Nan: Wynn? She snored under that cart from dark to dawn. I'd swear to it. I'd rather not have had to hear it.

actions.label: What happened?
actions.text:
Dace: Carter offered a coin to whoever proved the line. Marker said open. So I took the skiff out at first light, straight down the line.
Halfway over, something tore the bottom out of her. Like running onto a row of teeth. Under the water. Never saw it.
Waded back. She's still out there, stuck on whatever it was.

actions.label: Can I see the order?
actions.text:
Wynn: Here. Read it yourself. Avery's read it to me four times.
To the keeper at Whisperflow. Grain under emergency provision, for the households of the far bank. The Whisperflow marker reads open. The load is to cross on arrival, without delay.
Wynn: Handed to me at Crestbridge yesterday noon. Why?

actions.label: Do you work this bank often?
actions.text: Tovin: Brookhollow docks, mostly. Here when there's loading. Years now.

actions.label: Have you noticed anything odd about the markers?
actions.text: Tovin: ...No. Why would I?

actions.label: You hesitated. What is it?
actions.text:
Tovin: It's nothing. It's me. I draw things. Bends. Floors. It keeps my head straight.
This is here. Years back. The old post stood further up, by the bend. There's a mark under it.
I drew it because it looked like the notch. Like it was copying the notch.
Water used to sit funny there. Don't tell Maelin I said that.

actions.label: Inspect the notch
actions.text: The notch is cut a hand higher than on the grey posts. The water sits just under it.

actions.label: Inspect the footing
actions.text: The earth at the base is fresh and boot-tamped. No silt line on the wood. This went in overnight.

actions.label: Inspect drag marks
actions.text: Two furrows run upstream into the reeds. Something heavy was dragged.

actions.label: Pick up the weathered post
actions.text: A grey marker post, snapped at the base. Its notch matches the others on the bank.

actions.label: Clear the silt
actions.text: Older than the post. Older than the pier. The notch sits exactly where the grey posts' notches sit.

actions.label: Someone snapped the old post.
actions.text:
Maelin: Pulled out and snapped. Somebody wanted it gone, not moved. That one's finished.
Coppice is up the bank. Cut me a straight stem, a wrist and a half thick. Only the ribboned stools. The rest are growing.
No blade? Here. Crew hatchet. Bring it back sharp.

actions.label: Cut a marker stem
actions.text: A straight marker stem, cut from a ribboned stool.

actions.label: Cut the notch
actions.text: The stone's notch is the guide.

actions.label: What was that?
actions.text:
Maelin: ...It's done that before. Never where anyone was looking.
The river reading its mark.
Water's at the notch. Crossing's shut. Same as I've said since dawn. Go and show Avery his notch.

actions.label: Here's the old post. Compare the notches.
actions.text: Hollis: That's... a hand. That's a whole hand.

actions.label: Walk down to the bank and look for yourself.
actions.text: Hollis: The earth's fresh. No silt line. Fine. Fine.

actions.label: The post was grey at dusk and yellow at dawn.
actions.text:
Hollis: Mistress Ferrin doesn't sleep?
Nan: Not since before you were born, young man.

actions.label: The order was written before it was true.
actions.text: Hollis: Written before it was true. Someone knew what the post would say before the post said it.

actions.label: Tovin's sketch shows the old position.
actions.text:
Hollis: Pell? He's never said three words to me.
Tovin: You never asked.

actions.label: The marked line runs over a drowned pier.
actions.text:
Hollis: There's a pier there? It isn't on my sheet.
Maelin: It's on mine.

actions.label: Show the two proofs
actions.text:
Hollis: Whisperflow crossing is shut. By the keepers, by the river. Until the true post reads clear.
Maelin: Go up. River's rising. Everyone to the high landing before dark, and the grain with us.

actions.label: Take the dispatch order
actions.text: Wynn hands over the dispatch order.

actions.label: Lift grain sack 1
actions.text: Wynn: Mind that one, it's split. No, the other. Fine, it's both.

actions.label: Set down grain sack 1
actions.text: Grain moved above the flood line.

actions.label: Lift grain sack 2
actions.text: Wynn: Mind that one, it's split. No, the other. Fine, it's both.

actions.label: Set down grain sack 2
actions.text: Grain moved above the flood line.

actions.label: Lift grain sack 3
actions.text: Wynn: Boar! It's in the sacks!

actions.label: Set down grain sack 3
actions.text: Grain moved above the flood line.

actions.label: Help carry Nan's trunk
actions.text: Nan: Slowly. My mother's good plates are in there. Plate.

actions.label: Set down Nan's trunk
actions.text: Nan and Duchess are above the flood line.

actions.label: Check people and stores
actions.text: Maelin: Nobody stays on the low bank tonight.

actions.label: Put it in the keepers' record, Hollis.
actions.text:
Hollis: Thank you. It goes to Crest Hall at first light, with your name in it.
Maelin: Paper's slow. Hope it's honest.

actions.label: Take it, Maelin. Check the other markers.
actions.text:
Maelin: Every one, before the week's out.
Hollis: Then I'll log the closure. Not the cause. As far as Crest Hall knows, it never happened.

actions.label: I'll keep it until someone can tell me who wrote that order.
actions.text:
Maelin: Then don't lose it.
Hollis: You're not a keeper. ...But I suppose you're not wrong, either.

actions.label: Everyone who crosses here should know it's there.
actions.text: Maelin: All right. It's a good stone. People should know where the river keeps its mark.

actions.label: Leave it under the post. The post does the job.
actions.text: Maelin: That's what my teacher said. I'll have the crews look under the other old posts. Quietly.

actions.label: Good night, Maelin.
actions.text:
Maelin: River'll fall by morning. When the true post reads clear, I'll take you across. First, before the grain.
You read the bank before you read the paper. Most don't.
Sleep. I'll wake you when it reads clear. River keep you.

actions.label: Has the water been heavy lately?
actions.text:
Ansel: Stillwater's been thick as wool all week. Some nights I can't see my own lantern.
Two bends ran wrong this month. Water turning back on itself, like it forgot which way it was going.
Not here, mind. Here's always been a good bend.

actions.label: It was real. It wasn't you.
actions.text: Tovin: ...Oh. All right.

actions.label: Read the crossing marker
actions.text: Water's under the notch. The crossing reads open.

actions.label: Gather coppice timber
actions.text: Coppice timber gathered.

actions.label: Cook dried game strips
actions.text: Dried game strips prepared.

actions.label: Offer cooked food to the crowd
actions.text: Nan: Oh, you've done it properly. Duchess, look, someone's done it properly.

actions.label: Harvest game meat
actions.text: Game meat harvested.

actions.label: Harvest game meat
actions.text: Game meat harvested.

actions.label: Eat dried game strips
actions.text: You eat dried game strips.

actions.label: Inspect drowned pilings
actions.text: Black pilings just under the surface. An old pier. The yellow post's line runs straight across them.

actions.label: Inspect the dry groove
actions.text: The groove is dry. The notch is level with the post's.

actions.label: Compare Tovin's sketch
actions.text: It's the mark from Tovin's sketch.

actions.label: Read the true marker
actions.text: Water's over the notch. The crossing reads shut.

actions.label: What happens to the keepers' report?
actions.text: Maelin: Avery's rider goes at first light. We'll see what Crest Hall does with honesty.

actions.label: Will the crews check the other bends?
actions.text: Maelin: Crews start at the next bend tomorrow. Come along if you like. You've got the eye.

actions.label: I'm still holding the proof.
actions.text: Maelin: You've still got that post. Don't burn it for warmth.

actions.label: Who moved the post, Maelin?
actions.text:
Maelin: Somebody who knew the rule. That's what bothers me.
Anyone can lie with paper. You have to know a river to lie with a post.

actions.label: What's across the river?
actions.text: Maelin: Fields. People waiting on grain. More river. More posts.

actions.label: How did you record it?
actions.text: Hollis: I've written it down. All of it. I've never written anything that mattered before.

actions.label: What does the closure record say?
actions.text: Hollis: Closure logged. Cause: river. Which is true, I suppose.

actions.label: I'll keep the post safe.
actions.text: Hollis: If you lose that post, I'll have to pretend I never saw it. I'm bad at pretending.

actions.label: What's that tune?
actions.text:
Nan: My mam's. She called it the listeners' tune. Sang it at the water before a crossing, with the rhyme.
Never asked who the listeners were. You don't, when you're small. And then they're gone and you can't.

actions.label: Sit by the fire.
actions.text:
Dace: ...I'm sorry about the skiff.
Maelin: I know. Eat.

actions.label: How are you, Dace?
actions.text: Dace: Don't. I know.

actions.label: The grain is safe.
actions.text: Wynn: Forty sacks. Dry. Uphill. Not one eaten by a pig. I'll take it.

actions.label: Show me where you measured, Tamsin.
actions.text:
Tamsin: Don't stand there. That's the bad bit. I measured.
Upper household: That child's been out with that cord all week. We've stakes to set before the planting.
Lower household: And I've a boat that won't get past that tree. Every day it's 'wait'.
Tamsin: Fine. But you hold it how I say.

actions.label: I'll need an axe if there's cutting.
actions.text: Upper household: There's the bank axe. Bring it back. Or don't. It's older than me.

actions.label: Measure at the first knot
actions.text:
Tamsin: Flat to the bank. Flat. Now push. See?
The cord goes in a hand.

actions.label: Check your grip
actions.text: Tamsin: Not like that. Like you're holding a bird.

actions.label: Measure at the second knot
actions.text: Tamsin: That's a forearm. Banks aren't supposed to have forearms in them.

actions.label: Measure at the third knot
actions.text: Tamsin: Arm. Whole arm. I didn't tell them it was a whole arm. They'd have said I made it up.

actions.label: Inspect the wrack line
actions.text:
Reed and flood trash in the branches, above head height.
Tamsin: That's where the water got to. Higher than anyone says. I checked twice.

actions.label: Inspect the old repair face
actions.text: Weathered stakes, each with the same cut-mark. Wattle rotted between them. Somebody kept this bank once.

actions.label: Cut the jam's key limb
actions.text: The jam groans and shudders. Stand clear of its swing.

actions.label: Inspect the old cord
actions.text:
A measuring cord, green with age, tied off at the same marks as Tamsin's. Someone measured this bank the same way, a long time ago.
Tamsin: That's my knots. That's how I tie it. Every arm-span, double, then the hitch.
Somebody else worked it out too, then.

actions.label: Inspect the leaner
actions.text: Root plate cracked through. It's leaning further than it was.

actions.label: Inspect the holder
actions.text: Healthy. Its roots run straight across the hollow, like ribs.

actions.label: Inspect the old one
actions.text: Hollow, full of nesting holes. Holding nothing up but birds.

actions.label: Cut the leaner's notch
actions.text: A chalk line marks the fall.

actions.label: Back-cut the failing tree
actions.text: The crown sways. Stand clear of the chalked fall line.

actions.label: Leave it. Its roots are the bank.
actions.text:
Lower household: So we carry it. Again. Fine. Fine.
Upper household: I'll help you carry it. Some mornings.

actions.label: Take it down. They need the landing.
actions.text:
Upper household: Then I'll move my fence back before it moves itself.
Tamsin: It'll slump. Not today. When the water's next high. I'm only saying.

actions.label: Keep it. I'll build them a landing from the leaner.
actions.text:
Lower household: A landing. Below the tree. That'd do. That would actually do.
Tamsin: Put it on the downstream side. The upstream side's where it scours.

actions.label: Cut the holder's notch
actions.text: The roots span the hollow.

actions.label: Back-cut the holder
actions.text: The lower landing is clear.

actions.label: Cut the leaner's remaining limbs
actions.text: Sound wood for a landing stage.

actions.label: Give wood for the landing
actions.text: The wood is set beside the holder.

actions.label: Seat the first stage support
actions.text: The downstream support is seated.

actions.label: Seat the second stage support
actions.text: The landing stage sits below the holder.

actions.label: Tamsin. Tamsin's careful.
actions.text:
Upper household: Well. The cord was right.
Lower household: And who measures it next spring?
Upper household: Tamsin, then. Every spring. And you tell us, and we listen, and that's that.
Tamsin: You held it nearly right, by the end.

actions.label: How is the landing?
actions.text: Lower household: Still carrying the boat. Still here.

actions.label: How is the new stage?
actions.text: Lower household: Landing's good. Tamsin inspects it. Weekly.

actions.label: Have you measured anything else?
actions.text: Tamsin: I measured the docks. Don't stand on the third plank.

stages.objective: Find out why the crossing has stopped.
Hear both sides at the tollpost.
Clear the silt from the old footing.
Cut a new marker post from the coppice.
Set the new post on the old stone.
Show Hollis what the river says.
Help move the waiting people and grain to the high landing.
Speak with Maelin by the fire.
Find out why the bank is staked.
Walk the bank with Tamsin's cord.
Cut the driftroot jam free. Stand clear as it swings.
Inspect the three driftroots, then bring down the failing tree.
Decide which trees stay. Finish any cutting or landing work.
Tell the households what the bank needs.
